supported_claims.proposition: A patient's consent generally makes invasive medical treatment lawful, and treating a capacitous patient who refuses is unlawful.
supported_claims.exact_normalized_span_text: Generally it is the patient’s consent which makes invasive medical treatment lawful. It is not lawful to treat a patient who has capacity and refuses that treatment.

supported_claims.proposition: Nothing less than the clearest statutory wording will suffice to exclude judicial review altogether.
supported_claims.exact_normalized_span_text: I shall return below, under the second issue, to the question in what circumstances if any Parliament could exclude review altogether. There is no doubt that, if it is to be done, nothing less than the clearest wording will suffice (see De Smith para 1-027).

supported_claims.proposition: Equitable tracing rules have traditionally permitted tracing into a mixed fund.
supported_claims.exact_normalized_span_text: The equitable tracing rules have traditionally been understood to be less restrictive than the common law tracing rules (eg in permitting tracing into a mixed fund)

supported_claims.proposition: A knowing-receipt claim cannot succeed once the claimant's proprietary equitable interest in the property has been extinguished or overridden.
supported_claims.exact_normalized_span_text: They agree that a claim in knowing receipt cannot succeed once the claimant’s proprietary equitable interest in the property in question has been extinguished or overridden.

The judgment concerns accessory liability for intellectual-property torts, not unjust enrichment.

supported_claims.proposition: The English court's power to grant an anti-suit injunction derives from its general equitable jurisdiction under section 37 of the Senior Courts Act 1981, not only from powers supporting an existing or intended arbitration.
supported_claims.exact_normalized_span_text: In English law, however, it has been authoritatively established in AES Ust-Kamenogorsk that the source of the court’s power to grant anti- suit injunctions is not its jurisdiction to grant interim measures in support of current or intended arbitration proceedings but its general equitable jurisdiction under section 37 of the 1981 Act.

supported_claims.proposition: An anti-suit injunction enforces the arbitration agreement's negative promise not to litigate, whether or not arbitration is on foot or proposed.
supported_claims.exact_normalized_span_text: The purpose of issuing such an injunction is to enforce the negative promise contained in the arbitration agreement not to bring court proceedings, which applies and is enforceable regardless of whether or not any arbitration proceedings are on foot or proposed which require support.
